title: Pear and hazelnut cake
subtitle: a tender sponge with toasted hazelnuts and diced pear folded through the batter
excerpt: Pear and hazelnut cake is a moist sponge with toasted, roughly chopped hazelnuts and diced ripe pear folded through the batter. The pear gives moisture and a gentle fruity sweetness to the crumb; the hazelnuts add texture and a faint roasted note. The cake keeps well and is better the day after baking when the pear juices have distributed through the crumb.
sourceNotes: Pear and hazelnut as a flavour pairing documented in British and French baking traditions. Hazelnuts are native to Europe and were a common flavouring in northern European baking before almonds became widely available.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze whole, well wrapped, for up to 2 months. Defrost at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made the day before. Keeps at room temperature, covered, for 3 to 4 days.

content.text: Pear and hazelnut cake is a vanilla sponge with toasted hazelnuts and diced ripe pear folded through before baking. The pear gives the crumb a moist, gentle sweetness; the hazelnuts add crunch and a roasted note. Toast the hazelnuts first and rub off as much of the papery skin as you can before chopping them.

items.prepNote: ripe (Conference or Comice), peeled, cored, and diced 1 cm

content.text: Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease a 23 cm round cake tin and line the base with baking paper.

Toast the hazelnuts in a dry frying pan over a medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, tossing frequently, until the skins are cracking and the nuts smell toasted. Tip onto a cloth and rub off as much skin as possible. Leave to cool, then chop roughly.
Beat the butter and sugar together until pale and fluffy, about 3 to 4 minutes. Beat in the eggs one at a time and stir in the vanilla extract.
Fold in the flour until just combined. Fold in the hazelnuts and diced pear.
Spoon into the prepared tin and spread level. Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Leave to cool in the tin for 15 minutes before turning out onto a rack.

attrs.problem: Pear making the cake soggy in the middle
attrs.avoid: Avoid very soft, overripe pears; they release too much liquid during baking.
attrs.fix: Use firm pears and pat the diced pieces dry with kitchen paper before folding into the batter. If the pear is very juicy, add 1 extra tablespoon of flour to the batter.

attrs.problem: Hazelnuts sinking to the bottom of the cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid a loose batter; hazelnuts sink in thin batter.
attrs.fix: Toss the chopped hazelnuts in a teaspoon of flour before folding in. The flour coating helps them stay suspended in the batter during baking.
